items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Joe Williams would come in and sing with us. He’d come in and the minute he’d come in we’d go into “Rosetta” and he’d [scats] he’d come walking up from the bar and sing.

ctx.x: So you got into the Condon — picked up that Condon mantle or whatever it was. Did you enjoy your stint as a club owner?

Oh yeah. It was fantastic. I mean being in a center of my jazz world, owning, playing, band leading, managing and owning a club that represented everything I wanted to say, we didn’t have a cover charge, never had a music charge because when I grew up and © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

coming to New York I was able to go into jazz clubs and plunk myself down at the Metropole, order one beer and sit for three hours and listen to the greatest music possible. So in the face of all these stiff music charges that had been put on all the clubs in New York to quote pay for the music it’s made it become more elitist so that the average person can’t come in and listen to it and be influenced by the music.
